description: One offline CLI that diagnoses a repo the way four small tools do: context noise for AI agents, missing CLI commands, build-cache value, and flaky tests.
name: dev-diagnosis

prompts.description: Diagnose a repo before starting work in it: one full health check, the token-noise report, and the fix plan — without writing anything until the user agrees.
prompts.name: diagnose_repo
prompts.text: Diagnose the repo at "${arguments.path}" before starting work in it. Call diagnose_all with path "${arguments.path}" and report the overall score, the token-noise total, and the top noise items. If the context score is below 100, list the .aiignore entries the fix would add — call diagnose_context with fix: true and dryRun: true to preview them — and ask before writing anything: do not write .aiignore without the user agreeing.

tools.description: Find the files an AI coding agent should not read in a repo: build output, lockfiles, logs and oversized files.
tools.name: diagnose_context

tools.description: Check up the largest native binaries in a repo (ELF, PE, Mach-O): one hardening table each — PIE, NX, RELRO, stripped, stack protector, fortify, CET/BTI-PAC, RPATH, RUNPATH — plus whole-file entropy.
tools.name: diagnose_binaries

tools.description: Diagnose why a CLI command is missing: one row per shell context (current, login, non-login, daemon-like), shadowed copies, toolchain installs, and a copy-paste fix.
tools.name: diagnose_path

tools.description: Time one build command cold (cache moved aside) and warm (cache present) and say whether the cache pays.
tools.name: diagnose_cache

tools.description: Rank flaky tests from JUnit XML across CI runs, including passed-on-retry.
tools.name: diagnose_flakes

tools.description: Run every check that has what it needs and print one unified report: context runs (unless only/skip excludes it), path runs with a command name, flakes with a runs directory, cache with a build command.
tools.name: diagnose_all

tools.description: Scan named files for secrets only: the same content-level credential shapes the context check looks for (AWS keys, GitHub tokens, private keys, Slack tokens, high-entropy values assigned to a key-like name).
tools.name: diagnose_secrets
